summary: No official page found: the Town of Eads has no live website (townofeads.com and eadscolorado.com are parked), and nothing from the town describes overnight RV use of the roadside park. The only town source is Ordinance No. 414 (2023), a general rule for camping on any town property. Nothing changed; the aggregator-derived values (4 spots, free, 1-night max, no hookups) stay as they are, neither confirmed nor contradicted by an official page.
flags: DROP CANDIDATE (inclusion, like Del Norte Town Park in p3-165): this is a parking allowance, not a campground. On Esri imagery the park is a single crescent-shaped pull-off lot between US-287/CO-96 (E 15th St) and the railroad, with a restroom building, grass and picnic shelters; there are no marked or designated RV sites, pads or pedestals. No operator web presence at all: the town's domains are parked, no website is stored, and the inclusion rests on Campendium/The Dyrt reviews ('park anywhere you want' from a restroom attendant). Fails the live-web-presence and designated-site tests in docs/campground-curation.md.

Town rule: Ordinance No. 414 of the Town of Eads (published Kiowa County Press 2023-10-20, first reading 2023-11-10) makes it unlawful 'to camp on any Town owned or maintained property either more than two (2) days or without receiving written permit authorization from the Town Clerk'; permits cost $15 and last two days. The wording is ambiguous (two days free vs a permit always required), and it contradicts the stored 'free, 1-night max' only if read strictly. Not applied; a human should decide whether overnight RV stays there are even lawful without a permit.
